title: Cisplatin and etoposide with radiotherapy for small-cell cervical cancer
schedule_label: Usually four 21-day cycles. Cisplatin is normally given on day 1 and etoposide on days 1–3. The consultant can select a 28-day interval. Radiation usually starts with cycle 1 but can start later for clinical reasons.
schedule_summary: Usually four 21-day cycles. Cisplatin is normally given on day 1 and etoposide on days 1–3. The consultant can select a 28-day interval. Radiation usually starts with cycle 1 but can start later for clinical reasons.
purpose: The team uses chemotherapy to treat the cancer throughout the body and radiotherapy to treat planned areas. Ask your specialist whether the aim in your case is cure or disease control.
indication_text: This pathway covers the cervical small-cell neuroendocrine cancer indication. The specialist team confirms the pathology, stage and local radiation plan.
administration_text: On the usual day 1, etoposide runs into a vein over about an hour and is followed by cisplatin over about an hour, with protective fluids. On days 2–3, etoposide is either infused or prescribed as capsules twice daily. The written plan states which route and whether cisplatin is split across three days.
monitoring_summary: Repeat blood, kidney and liver tests. Review infection, bleeding, fluid balance, hearing, nerve symptoms, radiation and the exact etoposide route.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.explanation: Blocks an enzyme that cells need to repair DNA while dividing. Rapidly dividing blood and hair cells can be affected too.
agents.mechanism: Blocks an enzyme that cells need to repair DNA while dividing. Rapidly dividing blood and hair cells can be affected too.
agents.watch: Call for fever, chills, bleeding or a sore mouth that prevents drinking. Report flushing or dizziness during an infusion.
visual: Blocks an enzyme that cells need to repair DNA while dividing. Rapidly dividing blood and hair cells can be affected too.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Attaches to DNA so cells struggle to copy and repair it. During radiotherapy this can increase damage to the cancer cells.
agents.mechanism: Attaches to DNA so cells struggle to copy and repair it. During radiotherapy this can increase damage to the cancer cells.
agents.watch: Call if you pass much less urine, cannot keep fluids down, or develop ringing ears, hearing changes or persistent tingling.

common_effects.title: What you may notice
common_effects.text: Hair loss, tiredness, reduced appetite, nausea and a sore mouth may occur. Pelvic radiation can add diarrhoea or bladder irritation. Tell the team if drinking becomes difficult.

serious_effects.title: Low blood counts · Etoposide and cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Phone at once for fever, chills, sudden illness, unusual bruising or bleeding.

serious_effects.title: Hearing changes · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Tell the team about ringing or muffled hearing before the next treatment.

serious_effects.title: Kidney injury or dehydration · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Call if you pass little urine or vomiting stops you drinking.

serious_effects.title: Bowel, bladder and vaginal symptoms · Pelvic radiation
serious_effects.text: Report frequent diarrhoea, painful urination or bleeding. The radiation team can help with vaginal dryness and sexual health.

serious_effects.title: Sore mouth · Etoposide and cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report mouth soreness if eating or drinking is difficult.

phases.label: Day 1 · platinum and etoposide
phases.detail: Two drugs on day 1. Ask about the length of your hydration visit and your signed schedule for days 2 and 3.

phases.label: Days 2–3 · IV etoposide alone
phases.detail: Return for etoposide by drip if this is your prescribed route. Continue the dated anti-sickness course started on day 1.

phases.label: Days 2–3 · oral etoposide alone
phases.detail: Take the capsule strength and number on your label twice daily on the two prescribed days, on an empty stomach. If a dose is missed or vomited, phone the unit for advice before taking more.

phases.label: Days 2–3 · fractionated cisplatin with etoposide
phases.detail: A consultant may divide cisplatin across days 1–3. Return for fluids and cisplatin. The prescription separately states the route of etoposide.

questions.q: Does radiotherapy have to start on the first chemotherapy day?
questions.a: It often starts in the first cycle, but your radiation team may plan a later start. Keep both appointment lists and contact both teams about changes.

questions.q: Should I take capsules if I already had IV etoposide today?
questions.a: Check your written schedule. IV and oral doses on days 2 and 3 are alternative routes. Call the unit before taking a dose if the label and diary differ.

This combination is included in the Irish NCCP regimen for this rare cancer. The medicines do not have an Irish licence specifically for this use. Ask your consultant about the evidence, the alternatives and how the hospital reviews your plan.

support.title: Getting help
support.text: Call the 24-hour oncology number for fever, chills, unexplained bleeding, very little urine, uncontrolled vomiting or diarrhoea. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, breathlessness or faintness during an infusion.

teachback: Does radiotherapy have to start on the first chemotherapy day? Show where you will find your 24-hour contact number.
consent_support: In Ireland, using cisplatin with etoposide for small-cell cervical cancer is an off-label use. Your consultant will explain the evidence, risks and alternatives and ask for your consent under hospital policy. Discuss treatment intent and uncertainty in this rare cancer, alternative etoposide routes, kidney and hearing injury, marrow suppression, fertility preservation before pelvic therapy and longer-term pelvic effects.
safety_note: Call the 24-hour oncology number for fever, chills, unexplained bleeding, very little urine, uncontrolled vomiting or diarrhoea. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, breathlessness or faintness during an infusion.

evidence.title: Taiwanese Gynecologic Oncology Group · retrospective cervical cohort
evidence.interpretation: Specialist teams use platinum and etoposide for this rare cancer. A cervical cancer study looked back at earlier treatment records. It cannot tell exactly how much an individual will benefit.
evidence.limitations: Small retrospective subgroups, differing treatments and selection bias. The study used five or more cycles in one group. NCCP 00279 specifies four cycles. Lung cancer survival estimates and thoracic radiation schedules do not apply to this cervical pathway.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests. The team may formally measure kidney clearance or arrange hearing tests. Review nerve symptoms and pregnancy or fertility concerns.
Tell the team about ringing ears, hearing aids, tingling or previous platinum treatment.

rows.label: Before each cycle
cells: Repeat blood, kidney and liver tests. Review infection, bleeding, fluid balance, hearing, nerve symptoms, radiation and the exact etoposide route.
Bring your capsule pack if supplied and the signed medicine and radiation calendars.

rows.label: During and after the course
cells: The specialist team sets response assessment and follow-up around your stage and radiation treatment.
Report fever and new bleeding promptly. Ask about bowel, bladder and vaginal recovery, sexual health and menopause.

monitoring_schedule.note: The team individualises response assessments and extra tests according to symptoms and treatment aim.

prescription_phases.label: Day 1 · platinum and etoposide

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.timing: Up to three times daily · Subsequent days / as directed
medicines.note: Leave at least 6 hours between doses. Maximum 5 days and 30 mg/day or 0.5 mg/kg/day, whichever is lower. Review extrapyramidal risk with olanzapine.

additional_support: Use the dated anti-sickness prescription for the scheduled platinum treatment. Ask which dose to take next and how to use rescue medicine.
prescription_notes: Default is cisplatin 75 mg/m² on day 1. If the consultant selected fractionation or substituted carboplatin, reconcile the entire course and use the antiemetic schedule for the actual platinum.

prescription_phases.guidance: NCCP 00279 v8 and NCCP NCIS antiemetics, medical oncology

prescription_phases.label: Days 2–3 · IV etoposide alone
additional_support: Continue the signed anti-sickness course already started on day 1. Phone if you cannot drink or are unsure which dose is due.
prescription_notes: For the standard day-1 platinum course, reconcile prior antiemetics. Never restart the day-1 loading doses on return.

Continue the signed delayed antiemetic course from day 1, including rescue if prescribed. Check the dated prescription. Do not repeat loading doses. If cisplatin is also due today, use the fractionated cisplatin pathway.

prescription_phases.guidance: NCCP 00279 v8 and MASCC/ESMO multiday cisplatin guidance

prescription_phases.label: Days 2–3 · oral etoposide alone
additional_support: Follow the signed day-1 platinum anti-sickness course. The etoposide capsules themselves have low or minimal sickness risk. Ask the unit about rescue treatment if nausea persists.
prescription_notes: Confirm route, capsule strengths, calculation and dose count. Continue delayed-phase coverage from day 1.

Continue the signed delayed antiemetic course from day 1, including rescue if prescribed. Check the dated prescription. Do not repeat loading doses. If cisplatin is also due today, use the fractionated cisplatin pathway.

prescription_phases.label: Days 2–3 · fractionated cisplatin with etoposide

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.timing: Once daily · Days 1–3 before each cisplatin infusion

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.timing: Once daily · Days 2–5, enter dose after reviewing all steroids

additional_support: Use the dated anti-sickness prescription for the scheduled platinum treatment. Ask which dose to take next and how to use rescue medicine.
prescription_notes: For prescribed cisplatin 25 mg/m² on each of days 1–3, confirm the complete multiday course, including days after the last cisplatin. Verify the etoposide route separately.
Use a single course dated from the first cisplatin day. On days 2–3 check what was already taken and complete delayed protection through day 5. Reconcile rescue treatment and sedation before signing.
